courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Beginning German I
courses.description: Introductory course focusing on listening comprehension, oral skills, reading, writing, and culture.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Beginning German II
courses.description: Continuation of GER 101. Continued focus on listening comprehension, oral skills, reading, writing, and culture at an introductory level.
courses.prereqText: One semester of college German or equivalent.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Freshman Honors Tutorial
courses.description: Study of selected topics on an individually arranged basis. Open only to honors majors or to Cohn Scholars and Associates. May be repeated once.
courses.prereqText: Consent of departmental honors advisor.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Undergraduate Open Seminar
courses.description: Credit: 1 to 5 hours. May be repeated.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: German Literature in Trans
courses.description: Introduction to German literature for students with no knowledge of German. Same as CWL 224. May be repeated if topics vary.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: German Popular Culture
courses.description: Introduction to the study of modern and contemporary german culture through examining examples of popular culture from the late-eighteenth century to the present. Looks at texts and films as a mirror and critique of modern German society. Topics to be discussed: nationalism, gender, ethnicity, minority cultures, Jewish life in Germany, German images of other cultures, etc. Course taught in English.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Intermediate German I
courses.description: Continuation of GER 102. Intermediate course focusing on listening comprehension, oral skills, reading, writing, and culture. Credit is not given toward graduation for: GER 103 and GER 203.
courses.prereqText: Two semesters of college German or equivalent.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Intermediate German II
courses.description: Continuation of GER 203. Continued focus on listening comprehension, oral skills, reading, writing, and culture at an intermediate level. Credit is not given toward graduation for: GER 104 and GER 204.
courses.prereqText: Three semesters of college German or equivalent.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Germany and Europe
courses.description: Introduction into major issues in contemporary German society with a special focus on Germany's functioning within Europe and the European Union through novels, films, essays, interviews etc. Course taught in English.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Conversation and Writing I
courses.prereqText: GER 104 or equivalent, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Conversation and Writing II
courses.description: Continuation of GER 211.
courses.prereqText: GER 211 or equivalent, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Grimms' Fairy Tales - ACP
courses.description: Special attention is paid to the Grimms' tales in terms of traditional narrative genres, elements of life in early modern Europe, and versions from Italy and France as well as Germany. Course is conducted in English. Same as CWL 250 and ENGL 267. Credit is not given for both GER 250 and GER 251.
courses.prereqText: Completion of the Campus Composition I requirement.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Grimm's Fairy Tales in Context
courses.description: Special attention is paid to the Grimms' tales in terms of traditional narrative genres, elements of life in early modern Europe, and versions from Italy and France as well as Germany. Course is conducted in English. Same as CWL 254 and ENGL 266. Credit is not given for both GER 251 and GER 250.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: The Holocaust in Context - ACP
courses.description: Jewish contributions to German Literature from 1200 to the present day. Includes trips to the University Library's Rare Book Room. Same as CWL 271 and ENGL 268. Credit is not given for both GER 260 and GER 261.
courses.prereqText: Completion of the Campus Composition I general education requirement.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: The Holocaust in Context
courses.description: Examines cultural representations of the Holocaust in literature, film, and critical essays. Same as CWL 273, ENGL 269, and JS 261. Credit is not given for both GER 261 and GER 260.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Sexuality and Literature
courses.description: Examination of the historical contexts in which sexuality has been debated during the past three centuries, and to what extent sexuality is perceived differently in diverse cultures. Part one will look at the Western tradition, especially Germany. Part two will shift focus to the non-Western world, especially to the colonial history of Indonesia. Same as CWL 272 and GWS 270.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Study Abroad
courses.description: Lectures, seminars, and practical work in German language, literature, civilization, and in other academic areas appropriate to the student's course of study. Approved for letter and S/U grading. May be repeated in the same term to a maximum of 18 hours; may be repeated in separate terms to a maximum of 36 hours.
courses.prereqText: GER 104 or equivalent; 2.75 overall average; 3.0 average in German courses.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: German for Business
courses.description: Introduces German business language as used in basic operations in retail/wholesale, export/import, banking transactions.
courses.prereqText: GER 211 or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: German for Economics
courses.description: German language as used in professional contexts involving economic matters: texts and documents relating to forms of enterprises and their financing, to macroeconomic structures of domestic and foreign trade, and to reports on the economies of German-speaking countries.
courses.prereqText: GER 320 or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Intro to German Literature
courses.description: Introductory study of representative works (prose, drama, lyric) by outstanding German, Austrian, and Swiss writers of the modern period.
courses.prereqText: Two years of college German or equivalent.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: German Literature and Culture
courses.description: In German. Seminar in the literature and culture of German-speaking countries since 1750. Topic varies. Format: lecture; discussion; film screenings.
courses.prereqText: GER 331 or equivalent.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Politics of the European Union
courses.description: Considers the history of the European Union and its current functions and operations. Focuses on the ongoing process of political and cultural integration. Consists of sections in Illinois and abroad, interacting extensively via the worldwide web.
courses.prereqText: PS 240 or PS 241, six hours of Political Science credit, or consent of instructor; cross-listings require language training appropriate for enrollment in the respective overseas programs.
courses.pointerText: Same as EURO 385, FR 385, and PS 385. See PS 385.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Special Topics German Studies
courses.description: Introductory study in such topics as individual authors, selected literary movements or periods, modes of inquiry in literary study, minor genres, subgenres, extraliterary influences, etc. Same as CWL 328. May be repeated to a maximum of 6 hours if topics vary.
courses.prereqText: Reading fluency in German beyond the fourth-semester college level.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Global Issues in German
courses.description: Introduction to global issues in German media. Taught in German. 3 undergraduate hours. 3 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: GER 212 or equivalent.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: German-English Translation: Theory & Practice
courses.description: Theory and practice of translating technical, commercial, scientific, and literary texts from German into English and vice versa. Same as TRST 403. 3 undergraduate hours. 3 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: GER 401 or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: History of Translation
courses.description: Study of the historical development of translation ideas and practices in Europe and in particular cases across major global regions. Reading and analysis of key texts in the development of translation theory and case studies of practices and roles played by translation in different periods and geographical regions. Instruction in English. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.
courses.pointerText: Same as CLCV 430, CWL 430, ENGL 486, SLAV 430, SPAN 436, and TRST 431. See SLAV 430.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Language & Minorities in Europe
courses.description: Introduction to political, judicial, linguistic, and cultural issues concerning indigenous and migrant/immigrant languages in the countries of the European Union. Focuses on political and judicial issues, such as legal aspects of bilingual education and minority language use, as well as linguistic and cultural aspects, such as assimilation, language-mixing, and language change. Taught in English. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.
courses.pointerText: Same as EURO 418, FR 418, ITAL 418, LING 418, PS 418, SLAV 418, and SPAN 418. See FR 418.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: German Cultural History
courses.description: A general introduction to German culture from the pre-Christian period to the twenty-first century, focusing on the tension between forces of history and modernization in German culture. Course materials include literary and philosophical texts, film, painting, and music. Particular attention will be paid to the role of art in society. 4 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: One 200-level German course and GER 331; or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Multilingual Europe
courses.description: Exploration of multilingualism in the European context. Focus is on the historical, linguistic, cultural, and sociopolitical aspects of multilingualism across Europe. Topics include language policies and use in multinational institutions, language diversity, educational policies and practices, the role of English, and changing multilingualism in urban environments. 3 undergraduate hours. No graduate credit.
courses.prereqText: Students who received credit for GER 465 in Spring 2024 may not receive credit for GER 455.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Principles of Language Testing
courses.description: Studies theoretical and practical aspects of language testing. Examines purposes and types of language tests in relation to theories of language use and language teaching goals; discusses testing practices and procedures related to language teaching and language research; and includes the planning, writing, and administration of tests, basic descriptive statistics, and test analysis. A project is required. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: LING 489 or consent of instructor.
courses.pointerText: Same as EIL 460, EPSY 487, FR 460, ITAL 460, PORT 460, and SPAN 460. See EIL 460.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: German Linguistics
courses.description: Linguistic analysis of Germanic languages in historical, geographic, and social context. Taught in German or English, depending on topic. 3 undergraduate hours. 3 graduate hours. May be repeated in separate terms, as topics vary, to a maximum of 6 hours.
courses.prereqText: When the course is taught in English, there are no prerequisites. When the course is taught in German, the recommendation is GER 212 or consent of the instructor.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Middle Ages to Baroque
courses.description: Literary, thematic, cultural, and bibliographical analysis of the major authors, works, genres, and movements in German literature from 750-1720. Same as MDVL 470. 3 undergraduate hours. 3 graduate hours. May be repeated in separate terms to a maximum of 6 hours if topics vary.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Enlightenment to Romanticism
courses.description: Literary, thematic, cultural, and bibliographical analysis of the major authors, works, genres, and movements in German literature from 1720 to 1830. 3 undergraduate hours. 3 graduate hours. May be repeated to a maximum of 6 undergraduate hours or 6 graduate hours if topic varies.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Realism to Expressionism
courses.description: Literary, thematic, cultural, and bibliographical analysis of the major authors, works, genres, and movements in German literature from 1830 to 1920. 3 undergraduate hours. 3 graduate hours. May be repeated to a maximum of 6 undergraduate hours or 6 graduate hours if topic varies.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: 1920s to Today
courses.description: Literary, thematic, cultural, and bibliographical analysis of the major authors, works, genres, and movements in German literature from 1920 to the present. 3 undergraduate hours. 3 graduate hours. May be repeated to a maximum of 6 undergraduate hours or 6 graduate hours if topic varies.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Theoretical Foundations of SLA
courses.description: General introduction to second language acquisition (SLA) theory. Examines nativist, interactionist and cognitive approaches to SLA and explores the role of learner characteristics. Instruction in English. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: An introductory course in linguistics or consent of instructor.
courses.pointerText: Same as FR 481, ITAL 489, LING 489, PORT 489, and SPAN 489. See LING 489.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Honors Senior Thesis
courses.description: Intended primarily for candidates for honors in German, but open to other seniors. 1 to 4 undergraduate hours. No graduate credit. May be repeated to a maximum of 4 hours.
courses.prereqText: Senior standing; consent of instructor.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: German Cinema I
courses.description: Focus on the rise of German film from its earliest beginnings until 1945. Same as MACS 493. 3 undergraduate hours. 3 graduate hours.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: German Cinema II
courses.description: Study of German film from 1945 until the present. Same as MACS 494. 3 undergraduate hours. 3 graduate hours.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Special Topics German Studies
courses.description: Intensive study of restricted topics in German language, literature, and culture. 3 undergraduate hours. 3 graduate hours. May be repeated as topics vary to a maximum of 9 undergraduate hours or 8 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: Three years of college German or equivalent.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Readings in German Grads I
courses.description: Introduction to the reading of German texts in the sciences and the humanities. Credit is not given towards a graduate degree.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Readings in German Grads II
courses.description: Designed for graduate students preparing for the German reading requirements for the Ph.D. Credit is not given towards a graduate degree.
courses.prereqText: GER 500 or equivalent.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Introduction to Graduate Study
courses.description: Bibliography and methodology of the study of the Germanic languages and literatures, with particular regard to German literature and Germanic linguistics; introduction to scholarship in general and the German profession in particular, including the modes and methods of scholarly endeavor.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Applied Literary Translation I
courses.description: Focuses on both the theory and the practice of literary translation, as well as the business aspect of how to negotiate a translation proposal through the US publishing market. Students will produce a completed translation of a short story or a selection of poems.
courses.pointerText: Same as CWL 511, EALC 511, SLAV 501, and TRST 501. See TRST 501.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Applied LiteraryTranslation II
courses.description: Focuses on the practice and strategies of literary translation through the study of what prominent and successful translators have written about their own experience and through comparative analysis of prize-winning translations. Students will be exposed to reader response theory and the role of the translator as cultural agent while learning how to produce paratext for their translations (prefaces, notes, etc.) and developing skills in translation, editing, grant-writing, and participation in professional associations.
courses.prereqText: TRST 501 or consent of unit.
courses.pointerText: Same as CWL 512, EALC 512, SLAV 502, and TRST 502. See TRST 502.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Middle High German
courses.description: Same as MDVL 515.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: History of the German Language
courses.description: Internal and external history of German from prehistoric times to the present.
courses.prereqText: GER 465 or equivalent.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Old High German
courses.description: Grammar and interpretation of the oldest literary documents. Same as MDVL 530.
courses.prereqText: GER 465.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Modern Critical Theory
courses.description: Comprehensive introduction to the foundational thinkers, texts, and schools that orient contemporary work in the humanities, from German Idealism to Cultural Studies, Queer Theory, and Postcolonial Theory, among others. The course is intended primarily for beginning graduate students, but also for those who feel they have not covered the development of critical theory in a systematic way. The course will include significant discussion of figures including: Kant, Hegel, Marx, Nietzsche, Freud, Adorno, Lacan, Derrida, Foucault, Said, Spivak. Among the topics we will address are: history, the subject, aesthetics, value, power, language, ideology, materiality, gender, sexuality, race, and technology/media studies.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Medieval German Studies
courses.description: Seminar in selected genres, themes, or authors of the Middle Ages. Epic, lyric, and didactic works in prose and verse are read in the original language. Same as MDVL 571. May be repeated to a maximum of 12 hours if topics vary.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Early Modern German Studies
courses.description: Seminar in selected genres, themes, or authors of the early modern period (1500-1700). May be repeated to a maximum of 12 hours if topics vary.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: 18thC German Studies
courses.description: Seminar in selected genres, themes, or authors of the eighteenth century. May be repeated in separate semesters to a maximum of 12 hours if topics vary.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: 19thC German Studies
courses.description: Seminar in selected genres, themes, or authors of the nineteenth century. May be repeated in separate semesters to a maximum of 12 hours if topics vary.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: 20thC German Studies
courses.description: Seminar in selected genres, themes, or authors of the twentieth century. May be repeated in separate semesters to a maximum of 12 hours if topics vary.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Open Seminar in German Studies
courses.description: Seminar in literary phenomena (such as movements, genres and forms, relations, themes and types, interdisciplinary studies, women's studies) that go beyond the confines of a particular century. May be repeated in separate semesters to a maximum of 12 hours if topics vary.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Classroom Language Acquisition
courses.description: Provides for an introduction to the context, process(es), and product of classroom language acquisition; emphasis is placed upon research, research findings, and implications of research.
courses.prereqText: FLTE 471 or equivalent, or consent of instructor.
courses.pointerText: Same as EIL 580, FR 580, ITAL 580, PORT 580, and SPAN 580. See SPAN 580.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: German Language Teaching
courses.description: In-depth exploration of fundamental concepts of teaching German at the college level; designed for Teaching Assistants. Topics include teaching approaches, lesson planning, vocabulary, grammar, listening, speaking, reading, writing, culture, assessment, instructional technology, and curriculum design.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Theories in Second Language Acquisition
courses.description: Course introduces doctoral students to current mainstream theories (e.g., linguistic, psycholinguistic, cognitive, and social) used in SLA research. Emphasis is on gaining fundamental understanding of how theories work in SLA, how to evaluate them, and what they attempt to explain.
courses.prereqText: LING 489 or equivalent or consent of instructor.
courses.pointerText: Same as CI 584, EALC 584, EPSY 563, FR 584, ITAL 584, LING 584, PORT 584, and SPAN 584. See SPAN 584.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Sem Second Lang Learn
courses.description: Treats specific topics in second language learning that are of current research and/or theoretical interest. Topics vary from term to term. May be repeated to a maximum of 16 hours if topics vary.
courses.prereqText: SPAN 580 or equivalent or consent of instructor.
courses.pointerText: Same as EALC 588, FR 588, ITAL 588, LING 588, PORT 588, and SPAN 588. See SPAN 588.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Research in Special Topics
courses.description: May be repeated to a maximum of 8 hours.

courses.subject: GER
courses.title: Thesis Research
courses.description: Approved for S/U grading only. May be repeated in the same term or in separate terms.
